editorialReading: The hemisphere's nitrogen benchmark has reset sharply upward this week. The August Yara–Mosaic Tampa CFR ammonia contract has been confirmed at approximately $870/t — up $70/t on July's already-elevated $800/t — marking the highest Tampa settlement in this Hormuz-disruption cycle and setting the cost reference for the second-half US application season at a level that will flow through to corn-belt ammonia spot and DAP derivatives over the coming weeks. TTF front-month fell to ~€54.58/MWh on 4 August before recovering toward €57–59 on 5 August — a minor easing that offers no structural relief when the Western Hemisphere's own ammonia benchmark has just reset $70 higher. Urea is consolidating near $450–475/t (Egypt FOB, Aug-26 futures ~$475/t), well above any pre-Hormuz baseline; the mid-July trough of ~$385–400 now appears to have been the floor for this leg. DAP holds near $755–760/st on the CME NOLA curve, supported by China's phosphate export restrictions running through August. Brazil continues buying potash at ~$405–415/t CFR granular, broadly unchanged, as Safrinha crop preparation advances. The structural exposure for import-dependent Central American and Andean markets intensifies: the August Tampa fix at $870/t means hemisphere nitrogen access costs are moving higher, not lower, into the second-half planting season.
watchNext: Whether the August Tampa ammonia fix at ~$870/t propagates into US corn-belt ammonia spot and second-half application economics — and whether September's contract extends the Hormuz-cycle high. Whether urea sustains near the top of the $450–475 range or resumes its recovery from the mid-July trough. Watch the CME DAP/urea curve for US buy-side sentiment, Brazilian potash CFR into the Safrinha, and TTF gas as the global nitrogen cost floor. The squeeze on hemisphere food security runs primarily through import-dependent neighbours' access to affordable nitrogen. Sourcing note: real-time Argus / Green Markets assessments are subscription-only and the free World Bank Pink Sheet lags ~a month — these are publicly-cited indications.
